unit.why: A short anecdote: the Rebbe of Neskhiz tells a householder to do something, the man fails to do it, and the rebbe rebukes him.
unit.boundary_note: Division ends with the heading 'מענין מקוה', which belongs to the next division.

stories.start_quote: פ״א ציוה מרן מנסכיז לבעה״ב אחד
stories.end_quote: שמאל שהוא ימין ובפרט שהוא ימין
stories.summary_en: The Rebbe of Neskhiz orders a householder to do something, probably for the community; the man holds back because he thinks not doing it is better, and the rebbe calls him a fool, citing 'lo tasur' even when told left is right.

tags.why: The householder does not carry out the tsaddik's instruction.

quotes: אפילו כשאומר לך על שמאל שהוא ימין
tags.why: The point is that one must obey the tsaddik even against one's own judgment.
The rebbe justifies the duty to obey with the halakhic principle of 'lo tasur'.
The negative commandment not to stray from the sages' words is invoked.
The rebbe answers with a sharp rebuke.

missing_concepts: obedience to the sages' instructions even against one's own judgment (emunat chakhamim)
